name: half-division-of-every-pair-of-half-values-hashed-per-dividend
rationale: Metal's half division x / y for all 2^32 pairs of half bit patterns, without fast math: every quotient rounded once from the exact one, half denormals kept, and zeros, infinities and NaNs (every NaN folded to 0x7E00, since which NaN Metal answers is not in question). A 1024 x 1024 grid: the lane at (c, r) divides the half whose bits are 64 r + c / 16 by the 4096 halves whose bits start at 4096 (c mod 16), in loops whose bounds are the constants 4 and 1024 (no input bounds them), and atomically adds the FNV-1a hash of the quotients' bits to out at the dividend's bits (zero-initialized). Each hash step is a bijection of the previous hash, so any one quotient that differs changes its lane's hash and the dividend's sum; the sum does not depend on the order of the adds. The exhaustive check of a half division routine: quotients of two half values come within two float ulp of a half rounding midpoint, and denormal quotients hit midpoints exactly.

name: imageblock-scaled-tile-colour-plane
rationale: A tile twice the threadgroup in each axis: 8x8 threads staging a 2x2 block of imageblock cells each, then copied out as two planes. air.write_imageblock_slice_to_texture_2d.i16.v4f32 (7 case-less corpus sources) and air.write_imageblock_slice_to_texture_2d.i16.f32 (4), 11 sources. Every other authored imageblock case owns one cell per thread, which made the threadgroup extent and the imageblock extent the same number and let three separate places assume it; here the tile is 16x16 and the threadgroup is 8x8, so a lowering that linearised the tile by the threadgroup width lands cells (0,1) and (8,0) on one index and one that took the implicit slice region from the threadgroup extent copies the top-left 8x8 corner of a block Metal copies whole. The colour is (X, Y, X/2, Y/4) and the weight is X + 16Y at cell (X, Y), so each of the 256 cells holds a value that exists nowhere else in the tile, the four colour channels scale differently so a transpose or swizzle lands a quadruple that exists nowhere at all, and the two planes have different widths in the cell so a stride taken from the cell rather than the plane cannot satisfy both; a quarter-sized copy leaves 192 of the 256 texels at their authored poison. Every value is exact in binary32. Both slice regions are implicit, the form that has to derive the extent rather than read it. The dispatch is exactly one 8x8 threadgroup, so exactly one tile exists and the copy has no second threadgroup to race. The 32-byte cell puts 256 of them at 8 KiB, half the threadgroup memory Vulkan guarantees. This case compares the four-channel plane.

name: a-simdgroup-sum-ahead-of-a-discard-counts-only-the-kept-quad
rationale: The generated passthrough vertex draws the fullscreen triangle over an 8x4 rgba32_sint target, single-sampled, every pixel covered and every aligned 2x2 quad full. Buffer 0 (kept_quads) is 1: bit (y / 2) * 4 + x / 2 keeps the quad of pixels (0..2, 0..2), and every other quad is discarded whole; buffer 1 (k) is 0. The function takes before = simd_sum(1) ahead of if (!quad_kept && ...) discard_fragment(), then after = simd_sum(k + 1) and kept = simd_sum(quad_kept ? k + 1 : 0) after it, and a kept thread writes (before > after, after - kept, (before - after) & 3, before < after): values that hold however a device packs quads into simdgroups. DESIGN D327 item 6: Metal's compiler moves the sum past the discard, whose condition reads nothing of it, so it counts only the lanes that survive: Apple M4 and M3 Max write (0, 0, 0, 0) at the kept quad's four pixels from the fixture's AIR and from source (EVs REF-hfix, REF-hfix-m3), and the engine moves the sum there too (SEMANTICS 1094). The other 28 pixels keep the 0xab fill. A change in Apple's compiler that kept the sum ahead of the discard writes (1, 0, 0, 0) wherever a dropped quad shares the kept quad's simdgroup, and fails the case. Expected at pixels (0..2, 0..2): (0, 0, 0, 0).

name: an-atomic-between-a-simdgroup-sum-and-a-discard-keeps-the-dropped-quads
rationale: The generated passthrough vertex draws the fullscreen triangle over an 8x4 rgba32_sint target, single-sampled, every pixel covered and every aligned 2x2 quad full. Buffer 0 (kept_quads) is 1: bit (y / 2) * 4 + x / 2 keeps the quad of pixels (0..2, 0..2), and every other quad is discarded whole; buffer 1 (k) is 0. The function takes before = simd_sum(1) ahead of if (!quad_kept && ...) discard_fragment(), then after = simd_sum(k + 1) and kept = simd_sum(quad_kept ? k + 1 : 0) after it, and a kept thread writes (before > after, after - kept, (before - after) & 3, before < after): values that hold however a device packs quads into simdgroups. DESIGN D327 item 6: an atomic_fetch_add on buffer 4 (atomic_int, zero) lies between the sum and the discard, which keeps the sum ahead of the discard: it counts the dropped quads that share the kept quad's simdgroup, and Apple M4 and M3 Max write (1, 0, 0, 0) at the kept quad's four pixels from the fixture's AIR and from source (EVs REF-hfix, REF-hfix-m3); the engine keeps it there too. The other 28 pixels keep the 0xab fill. A device whose fragment subgroup holds fewer than two quads (4-lane arm64 lavapipe) cannot place a dropped quad beside the kept one and writes (0, 0, 0, 0), a valid Metal answer for a partly occupied simdgroup: the C3 subgroup gap fragment_subgroup_under_two_quads. A change in Apple's compiler that moved the sum past the discard writes (0, 0, 0, 0) on Metal and fails the case. Expected at pixels (0..2, 0..2): (1, 0, 0, 0).

name: constant-half4-zero
rationale: The fragment entry ignores its position and no-perspective float2 varying inputs and returns literal half4 zero at color location zero; one full-coverage fragment must replace the complete poisoned pixel.

name: bounded-dynamic-visible-table-clear-slot-two-threadgroup-primary
rationale: The literal four-word size table [4, 0, 0, 0] bounds the only reachable loop: its induction starts at visible-table slot 2, increments once to 3, and exits because the masked first word minus one is exactly 3. One invocation takes the non-empty path because the authored bounds are float2(1), calls visible-function-table slot 2, and receives exact float4 zero from the linked _uber_clear body without dereferencing callback arguments. Eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds, with register 2 selected as the result. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel, which is selected for byte-exact comparison.

name: constant-half4-render-target
rationale: The parameter-free fragment entry returns a constant half4 to attachment zero; one full-coverage fragment must replace the complete poisoned RGBA16Float pixel.

name: primitive-acceleration-structure-word
rationale: One authored triangle builds a primitive acceleration structure on Metal while an unused Vulkan handle consumes no descriptor; the kernel writes a poisoned output deterministically.

name: reset-indirect-entry-count
rationale: The loop-free entry ignores its grid index and unconditionally replaces the complete poisoned four-byte indirect-entry counter with aligned i32 zero.

name: one-simdgroup-minimum-of-thirty-two-descending-integers
rationale: One threadgroup of thirty-two threads is exactly one SIMD group, so the first reduction spans every lane and the second sees the reduced value in slot zero against thirty-one FLT_MAX sentinels, which leaves it unchanged. The inputs descend by one from 100, so the minimum is 69 and it is reachable only if all thirty-two lanes take part: any lane the reduction misses raises the answer to 70 or more, and any half-width lane model gives 85. Every value is a small integer, so no ordering of the reduction can round.

name: four-points-of-two-instances-scale-and-bias
rationale: The render template the indirect-command render replay cases draw with (DESIGN D249), run on its own as a rasterization-disabled vertex function: params holds the scale 3 and the bias 5, and a point draw of 4 vertices and 2 instances writes params[0] * (vid + 1) + params[1] + 1000 * iid to out[16 * iid + vid], so out holds 8, 11, 14, 17 at words 0 to 3 and 1008, 1011, 1014, 1017 at words 16 to 19. Every other word keeps the 0xab fill, and every written byte differs from it.

name: dsm2-zero-sign-uniform-threadgroup-of-sixteen
rationale: DESIGN D278 (refining D271.9): a threadgroup of 16 runs the multiply-add in workgroup-uniform control flow; lanes 16-31 do not exist. Rows 0-1 read the absent lanes' zero z, rows 2-3 read -z. Inputs (S-): a is +1 everywhere except a[r][k] = -1 for rows 2-3, columns 4-7; b rows 0-3 are -0 and b rows 4-7 (the cells lanes 16-31 hold) are -0; c is -0. A whole simdgroup's result is -0 in rows 0, 1, 4-7 (every term -0) and +0 in rows 2-3 (-1 * -0 = +0). Rows 0-3 are held by lanes 0-15, and their terms in k = 4-7 multiply an a cell of lanes 0-15 by a b cell of lanes 16-31: if those b cells are a zero z, rows 0-1 read z * 1 = z and rows 2-3 read z * -1 = -z, every other term -0, so rows 0-1 are -0 and rows 2-3 +0 when z is -0, and the reverse when z is +0. Every value is +1, -1, +4, -4, or a signed zero, exact in float and half whatever the accumulation order, and a sum of signed zeros is -0 exactly when every term is. out[2g + j] is lane g's float cell j, out[2n + 2g + j] its half cell widened (n the grid's threads); a lane that does not run the multiply-add leaves its words at the 0xAB poison. Compiled without fast math. The AIR has no loop.

name: dsm2-zero-sign-uniform-threadgroup-of-sixteen-plus-zero-rows
rationale: DESIGN D278 (refining D271.9): dsm2-zero-sign-uniform-threadgroup-of-sixteen with input S+ (b rows 4-7 +0 in memory, which no existing lane loads): the same bytes unless the answer follows memory no lane loaded. Inputs (S+): input S- with b rows 4-7 (the cells lanes 16-31 hold) +0 in place of -0: a whole simdgroup's rows 0-1 and 4-7 are +0 and rows 2-3 -0. Where lanes 16-31 do not take part, rows 0-1 read z and rows 2-3 read -z for their zero cell z, the same bytes as under S- unless the multiply-add reads those lanes' loaded registers. Every value is +1, -1, +4, -4, or a signed zero, exact in float and half whatever the accumulation order, and a sum of signed zeros is -0 exactly when every term is. out[2g + j] is lane g's float cell j, out[2n + 2g + j] its half cell widened (n the grid's threads); a lane that does not run the multiply-add leaves its words at the 0xAB poison. Compiled without fast math. The AIR has no loop.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-nineteen-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 19 and receives exact float4 zero from all eighteen linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-one-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry swizzles it to float4(0,0,0,1), writes both required poisoned output textures, and captures binding zero byte-exactly.

name: linked-single-unit-column-write
rationale: All input, output, kernel, window, dilation, stride, and launched-thread extents are exactly one with zero padding. The channel, window-height, and window-width loops therefore each execute once; the exact linked prefix returns one and the direct destination accumulates that value into the sole poisoned float.

name: linked-k48-gather-quantized-matrix-multiply-rhs-bfloat-16-non-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry (DESIGN D296; WP-EVG, TODO 6.2), whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes (1 simdgroup) runs the single 16x16 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 16, K = 48 (one whole 32-deep block, the unsafe loader, and a 16-deep remainder, the safe one). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table. The indices select expert 0 for rows below 8 and expert 1 for the rest, so the kernel walks two row segments, each a full tile multiply over its expert (expert strides w, scales and biases batch stride = N*K = 768), writing only its own rows. W[e][k][n] (w_ld = 16 bytes): both experts hold q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (all 16 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads); expert 0's scales repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and expert 1's are half of them (biases unread without the bias bit). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48): rows of segment 0 hold a = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, rows of segment 1 hold 2a, so every row of the result is the same (2a . W/2 = a . W): the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 16 words observed (64 bytes) do not depend on write order, and a row given the other segment's expert would write another. Each dequantized weight is a multiple of 0.25 at most 30, exact in bfloat, and each x at most 10; each product with x a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-quantized-matrix-multiply-rhs-bfloat-16-non-transposed
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The non-transposed bfloat 16 counterpart of the committed mps_gather_qmm_rhs_t_bfloat_64 case (DESIGN D272): mps_gather_qmm_rhs_n_bfloat_16 with the same function constants, resources, one-thread dispatch, and linked visible functions (postfixPrimary_4xf, postfixPrimary_f). Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links translation units each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule (D272.4) and the matmul2d lowering (D272.3). Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: convert-four-uint-texel-pairs-to-half-at-their-own-pixel
rationale:
air.convert.f.v2f16.u.v2i32 had no authored case; 43 corpus sources sit behind it. The host reads two unsigned channels of a texel, converts them to half and scales them by half(0.001).

A fragment case cannot choose its varyings, but this shader's only stage-in is air.position, which is the fragment coordinate - the harness cannot move it, and truncating it to uint gives each fragment its own pixel index. So a 2x2 render target over a 2x2 uint texture gives four fragments that each read their own texel, and the case controls all eight numbers.

The eight are chosen against the two roundings in the path. Every one is exactly representable in half, so the convert itself is not where a difference can hide - what is tested is that the convert happens at all and on the right lanes. The scale then rounds: 1024 and 4096 land exactly on a half, and 2050, 255, 60000, 999 and 7 each round, with the nearest tie at least a quarter of a step away so a one-ULP disagreement between an implementation computing the product at half width and one widening to float cannot change the answer. Zero and 60000 put the pair four binades apart in the same fragment. The two channels the shader does not read hold 0xDEADBEEF and 0xFEEDFACE, so a swizzle that reaches past .rg is visible.

All thirty-two bytes were derived by hand; Metal and MoltenVK both answer them.

name: a-texture-selected-between-two-argument-buffer-members-is-the-selected-members
rationale: DESIGN D339 item 2: a texture chosen between two adjacent members of an argument buffer (cond ? m.second : m.first, the shape of two corpus rows) reaches AIR as a select of the two members' addresses, a 64-bit integer load of the chosen member's resource id, and an inttoptr of it back to the texture. Constant argument buffer 0 is Material {float scale = 2; texture2d<half> first (4x1, red 1, 2, 3, 4); texture2d<half> second (8x1, red 10..17)}. Thread t reads texel (t >> 1, 0) of second for an odd t and of first for an even t and writes red * scale + width: 6, 28, 8, 30, 10, 32, 12, 34. The two textures differ in width and in every texel read, so a translation that reads the other member, or one member for every thread, fails the words of the threads that chose the other.

name: reduce-a-four-by-four-blur-map-into-a-signed-atomic-min-and-max
rationale: Four gathers with offsets (1,1) (1,3) (3,1) (3,3) around pixel (0,0) cover the whole 4x4 texture exactly once, so the reduction is over all sixteen texels and independent of the order gather returns them in. The red channel carries multiples of 1/32 while green and blue carry +9 and -9, so gathering the wrong component misses by four orders of magnitude. The values are, so scaling by 65536 lands on integers and floor/ceil are exact. The extremes sit in opposite corners, so dropping any part of the footprint changes the answer. The min is negative and the max slot starts negative, so an unsigned atomic min or max would leave both slots at their seeds instead of reaching -16384 and 14336.

name: imageblock-views-read-b-and-n-into-the-color
rationale: Partial views of a master imageblock layout (DESIGN D187, D201): the fragment reads b and n through one view and writes a = b + 1, tag = (x, y, n & 255, n >> 8) and m = n + 1 through another whose own offsets differ from the master's. a shares its word with b and m with n, so a write that replaced the whole word would clobber the member the second of the two overlapping instances then reads. Observes the color (b, n, 0, 1) of the read view.
